score.note: As composed, take 1 keeps strict time but brings its big drop in at 36.25 s where this plan has it at 35.0 s, runs its drums to 49.4 s, and every hit sits 20 ms after the beat. tools/score_edit.py corrects all three and writes audio/music/score_cut1.wav, which the mix plays. Take 2 drifts to about 142 beats a minute in the drop and is not used.

score2.about: The score as recomposed on the eighth pass, after reading ElevenLabs' own guide to prompting music (decide genre, mood, instruments, tempo and era; speak in studio terms; narrate the arrangement; say what is banned). One continuous performance in six sections, every section a whole number of bars at 144 BPM, so that it can be cut to the picture on bar lines. The film does not play it straight through: tools/score_edit.py places each section where the cut wants it.

score2.verdict: Measured bar by bar on arrival (out/score2_report.txt): all three takes play one unbroken sub-bass groove for 37 to 40 seconds whatever the section asks for, with almost nothing above 4 kHz, bring the drop in one to two bars late and stop the drums two bars late. Asking for 'high' context adherence told every section to sound like its neighbours. Not used. The same measurement run on the score the film had until v010 shows the same thing: 33 seconds of sub bass with the highs 28 dB down. That is what was wrong with the music.

cues.about: The score as used from the eighth pass on: each passage of the film composed on its own from a plain prompt, written to ElevenLabs' guide (genre, mood, instruments, tempo and era all decided; studio words; what is banned said out loud). A model asked for one thing does it; asked for six sections in a row it played one groove throughout (see score2). Every cue is in D minor at 144 BPM so that they sit together, and every prompt asks for brightness, because the first score measured as sub bass and little else. tools/score_edit.py finds each cue's beat by measurement and lays it on the film's grid.

engine.prompt: Driving futuristic melodic techno, 144 BPM, D minor. Starts instantly at full energy on the first beat with no intro: punchy tight four-on-the-floor kick, crisp bright sixteenth-note hi-hats and sharp claps, a glassy plucked analog synth arpeggio racing in the high register, a growling mid-range bassline, tight sidechain pumping. Tense and urgent, sleek and modern, polished wide film-trailer production with sparkling highs. Instrumental only, no vocals.

under.prompt: Sparse futuristic underscore for dialogue, 144 BPM, D minor. No drums and no kick drum: just a soft glassy plucked synth arpeggio ticking quietly in the high register like a clock, one muted pulsing synth bass note on each beat, and a thin airy pad. Lots of empty space, patient suspended tension, clean and minimal, a sleek modern film score. It stays this sparse all the way through. Instrumental only, no vocals.

still.prompt: One soft warm synth pad chord in D minor held almost perfectly still, with a faint high glassy shimmer and air above it. No rhythm, no drums, no bass line, no melody. Intimate, suspended, fragile and hopeful. Ambient film score, close and quiet. Instrumental only, no vocals.

flood.prompt: Euphoric melodic techno drop for a film's climax, 144 BPM, D minor. Starts instantly at full energy on the first beat with no intro: huge four-on-the-floor kick, offbeat open hi-hats and fast breakbeat fills, deep driving sub bass, a bright wide-open sixteenth-note analog arpeggio, enormous supersaw chords, and a soaring wordless female choir holding sustained airy vowels. Sidechained, glassy, futuristic, wide and loud, triumphant and joyful. No sung words. It stays at full energy all the way through.

flood_lift.prompt: Euphoric futuristic melodic techno drop for a film's climax, 144 BPM, D minor. Starts instantly at full energy on the first beat with no intro: huge punchy four-on-the-floor kick, bright offbeat open hi-hats, crisp claps and fast breakbeat fills, a sparkling wide-open sixteenth-note analog arpeggio, enormous supersaw chords, and a soaring wordless female choir on sustained airy vowels. After four bars everything lifts: the chords climb higher and the choir opens up, even bigger and brighter. Sidechained, glassy, wide and loud, triumphant and joyful. No sung words, never drops in energy.

theme.prompt: Futuristic euphoric melodic techno with a cinematic choir, 144 BPM, D minor. The first eight bars (13 seconds) are just a sparkling sixteenth-note analog synth arpeggio, crisp ticking hi-hats and shakers, and an airy wordless female choir pad: no kick drum and no bass yet, restless and expectant. Then the drop hits at full energy and stays there to the end: huge punchy four-on-the-floor kick, deep driving bass, bright offbeat open hi-hats, claps and fast breakbeat fills, the arpeggio wide open, enormous supersaw chords, the choir soaring on sustained airy vowels. Glassy, sidechained, wide and loud, triumphant and joyful, polished modern film-trailer production. No sung words.

sfx2.about: The effects made again on the eighth pass with ElevenLabs' newer effects model (eleven_text_to_sound_v3; the first set was made with v2, which the vendor has since deprecated). Prompts follow the vendor's guide: the action, the setting and the performance, one sound at a time. Each file is measured when it arrives (tools/sound.py sfx2): how long the sound itself is, where its energy sits, and whether it is only rumble. The mix takes a sound from audio/sfx2/ when it is there and from audio/sfx/ when it is not.
